title: Strategic Account Commander Briefing and Renewal Blueprint
summary: A concise, two-track QBR template and renewal playbook for Strategic and Standard accounts. Emphasizes senior stakeholder narrative for Enterprise customers while providing a light-weight operational version for standard accounts. Includes slide-level speaker notes, a renewal tracker skeleton, risk-score rubric, and a worked example summary for a multi-product seat-upgrade renewal.
audience: Customer Success Managers, Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, Renewal Ops
objective: Provide a repeatable briefing artifact that (1) surfaces adoption and ROI with data-backed narratives, (2) clarifies renewal timing and asks by stakeholder, and (3) prescribes a concrete mitigation and escalation path when renewal risk > medium.
approach_overview: Two-track deck approach: 'Standard' (concise 8-slide flow for mid-market and high-velocity accounts) and 'Enterprise' (detailed 14-slide flow with exec story, TCO/ROI appendix, and multi-stakeholder playbook). Both tracks share a common risk rubric and renewal tracker to preserve consistency across renewals.
slide_outline: Title + Meeting Objective (1 slide) — quick framing: renewal horizon, decision-maker, ask
Executive Snapshot (1 slide) — net outcome statement (value realized, strategic alignment), C-level one-liner recommendation
Health at a Glance (1 slide) — adoption metrics, latency/cost KPIs, uptime, key integrations
Usage & Value Trends (1-2 slides) — 90/180/365 day trends, ARR impact by feature
Critical Wins & Customer Quotes (1 slide) — product wins mapped to business outcomes
Open Risks & Blockers (1 slide) — technical, adoption, procurement, legal
Renewal Ask & Options (1 slide) — recommended renewal tier, alternatives, pricing anchors
Renewal Timeline & Owners (1 slide) — dates, owners, gating items, final decision window
(Enterprise only) Stakeholder Map & Communication Plan (1 slide) — decision roles and tailored messages
(Enterprise only) Financial Appendix (1-2 slides) — TCO, ROI, seat-by-seat impact, savings from batching/quantization suggestions
(Enterprise only) Rollout & Support Commitments (1 slide) — SLA, dedicated onboarding milestones, escalation contacts
(Enterprise only) Pilot/Proof Points Appendix (1 slide) — experiments, eval prompts, eval pass/fail criteria
Next Steps & Success Plan (1 slide) — 30/60/90 day plan aligned to renewal goals
Appendix & Data Sources (1 slide) — queries, dashboards, linked tickets
speaker_notes_template: Title: State the purpose clearly and the desired decision at end of meeting.
Exec Snapshot: Start with the headline — what success looks like to their execs and how Redwood helped deliver it.
Health: Call out any anomalies and what we've done to mitigate them. Tie latency/cost regressions to root cause if known.
Usage Trends: Use 90/180-day windows. Highlight sticky features and churn signals (drop in session length, decline in embeddings usage).
Risks: Be explicit about procurement/legal blockers and suggest pull-through asks (technical POC, shortened trial for new units).
Ask Slide: Present 2 options (Recommended, Preserve, Contingency) and the business impact of each.
Timeline: End with the gating checklist and the first immediate action for both the CS and AE.
renewal_tracker_template: Columns: account-name | renewal-date | ACV | current-tier | recommended-action | risk-score | last-touch-date | next-step-owner | required-docs | procurement-status | legal-status | expected-decision. Use 'risk-score' (0-100) to drive automated alerts: >75 red, 50-75 amber, <50 green.
risk_scoring_rubric: Score components: Product Health (0-40), Commercial Signals (0-25), Engagement (0-20), External/Procurement Friction (0-15). Example thresholds: 0-49 low risk, 50-74 medium, 75-100 high. Product Health metrics: active seats growth, daily active users, errors per 1000 calls. Commercial Signals: usage-to-commit ratio, pending reversions, discount requests. Engagement: number of exec touchpoints past 90 days. External: procurement lead time >45 days, legal objections outstanding >30 days.
playbook_steps: 1) Diagnose: pull last 90-day dashboard, check open SRE incidents, get AE commercial notes. 2) Align: set internal pre-brief with AE/SE/Legal, map decision-makers. 3) Propose: prepare 2 rational pricing options and a short pilot/POC contingency. 4) Negotiate: define approval matrix and discount guardrails. 5) Close: confirm signed SOW, schedule onboarding milestones. 6) Post-close: 30/60/90 success plan delivered to customer and ops handoff to renewal ops.
escalation_matrix: Green: CS owns weekly cadence. Amber: CS+AE weekly plus solutions engineering involvement. Red: CS+AE+Head of CS+Sales Leader required, pull legal and finance to weekly steering until resolution.
worked_example_summary: Sample account 'Aquila Retail' — current ACV $320k, renewal in 60 days. Product health score 68, commercial signal 55, engagement 40, external friction 10 => total 173 normalized to 58 => medium risk. Recommendation: pursue 'Consolidate' tier with 10% multi-year commit credit; trigger exec sponsor call within 10 days; prepare a 30-day technical credit to unblock procurement. Tracked in renewal tracker row with owners: CS: Marissa, AE: Diego, Legal POC: Evelyn.
data_and_queries_notes: Primary data sources: usage dashboards (Prod-metrics), support tickets (Zendesk ID), billing ledger. Suggested queries: 1) monthly_active_users_by_feature.sql, 2) token_cost_trend.sql. Keep one slide to reference exact query names and dashboard IDs for reproducibility.
templates_and_assets: Attachables: slide master for both tracks (light and detailed), renewal-tracker CSV skeleton, exec-email cadence templates, sample SOW checklist, negotiation guardrail sheet.
next_actions: 1) Internal feedback loop: CS team to test template in two upcoming QBRs, collect usability notes by 2025-10-16. 2) Sync with Revenue Ops on automation of the renewal tracker by 2025-10-23. 3) Prepare Enterprise workshop facilitator notes for strategic accounts by 2025-11-01.
notes_to_self: Avoid slide overload. For enterprise, prioritize exec narrative and financing appendix. For standard accounts, keep to no more than 8 slides and a single recommended renewal path. Capture customer quotes early and secure a data snapshot 48 hours before the meeting.
